newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mostly higher in shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mostly higher in shortcovering.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mostly higher Thursday in some shortcovering ahead of the Easter holiday weekend, industry sources said.
Traders said the futures prices were moving higher on the strength of interest from several large buyers who were most likely covering short positions.
The futures strength was a bit of a surprise to some traders, however, who noted that physical electricity prices were moving lower.
"Cash prices are flat to down, and they are really down in the Northwest," said one Houston-based futures trader.

As of 1250 EST, NYMEX May Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 53 cents at $15.40 after morning exchanges as low as $14.60, while June was up 36 cents at $16.25 after reaching as low as $15.90 per megawatt hour (MWh).
PV summer deferreds were also up, with August 25 cents higher at $24.40 per MWh.

May California Oregon Border (COB) was up 22 cents at $10.70 per MWh after reaching as low as $10.40, while June COB was the only power futures contract trading lower, down three cents at $10.75 per MWh.
August COB was bid at $18.00 and offered at $18.30 from Wednesday's settle at $18.00 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1225 EST an estimated total of 68 COB and 140 PV contracts had traded.
NYMEX will close tomorrow in observance of Good Friday.
In power news, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington will be shut today, several weeks earlier than planned for maintenance due to ample hydropower in the region.
There was also talk of an outage at the 750 MW unit 2 at the Navajo coal-fire plant in Arizona lasting as long as two weeks, although the unit's status could not be confirmed.
Several units were planning to resume generation, with the 1,070 MW San Onofre unit 2 in southern California and the 1,221 MW Palo Verde unit 3 in Arizona scheduled to resume operations next week.

Capacity on the Pacific Intertie power transmission system, which links the Northwest to Southern California, will be raised to 6,250 megawatts by this weekend, if Bonneville Power Administration is successful in re-energizing the 500 KV John Day-Slatt line in Oregon.
In the Northwest, temperatures were forecast to remain near normal across the western part of the area for the rest of the week, and avarage slightly above normal in the south and east.
The Southwest would continue dry and warm into early next week with readings running four to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.

Weather Services Corp said Northwest cities like Portland and Seattle would see readings in the 50s through Saturday, while Southwest centers such as Los Angeles and Phoenix would experience temperatures in the 70s-80s.
COB open interest for March 26 fell 49 to 3,579 while PV open interest rose 35 to 3,299, NYMEX said.
